html:
The Valdivia earthquake of 22 May 1960 in southern Chile is the most powerful earthquake ever recorded, with a magnitude estimated between 9.4 and 9.6. The shaking lasted about ten minutes.

It struck where the Nazca Plate dives under South America, part of the Pacific Ring of Fire. A long stretch of fault, roughly a thousand kilometres, slipped at once. The city of Valdivia was hit hardest; land along the coast sank, and rivers and farms were flooded for good. Estimates of the dead in Chile range from about 1,000 to 6,000.

The quake set off a tsunami that crossed the whole Pacific Ocean. About fifteen hours later it killed 61 people in Hilo, Hawaii, and about a day later it struck Japan, killing around 140. It also hit the Philippines and New Zealand. Two days after the quake the Cordón Caulle volcano erupted.

The disaster led to better tsunami warnings across the Pacific. Chile, which sits on one of the world's most active plate boundaries, later built some of the strictest building codes anywhere.
sum: The Valdivia earthquake of 22 May 1960 in southern Chile is the most powerful earthquake ever recorded, with a magnitude estimated between 9.4 and 9.6. The shaking lasted about ten minutes.
